Filter Nesting Attempts Based on Expected Nest Phenological Periods

Source: R/nw.filterphenology.R
nw.filterphenology.Rd

To provide additional checks on data quality before analysis, an analyst may want to filter out nesting attempts which were recorded to have nesting phenologies of unexpectedly long lengths. This function allows an analyst to specify species-specific values for nest phenologies using expected days in the lay, incubation, nestling, and total nesting periods. By defining these allowable time frames an analyst can flag or remove "run-on" nest attempts or nests which do not match the specie's life history. This function only uses values for host eggs/young, and does not factor in brood parasite eggs or young.

Usage

nw.filterphenology(
  data,
  mode,
  max_phenology,
  trim_to_active = FALSE,
  output = NULL
)

Arguments

data

dataframe; A dataframe of merged NestWatch attempt and visits data. Date columns must have class Date and Datetime columns must have class POSIXct.

mode

"flag" or "remove"; A character string defining if the analyst wants the identified nesting attempts to be flagged with "FLAGGED" in a new column, or removed from the dataset.

max_phenology

dataframe; A simple dataframe with one row for each species of interest and the following column structure:

  • Species: The 6-letter species code for each species.

  • Lay: The number of days representing the maximum expected laying period for each species.

  • Incubation: The number of days representing the maximum expected incubation period (between clutch complete and hatch) for each species.

  • Nestling: The number of days representing the maximum expected nesting period (hatch and last fledge) for each species.

  • Total: The number of days representing the maximum expected total nesting period (spanning first initial nest building to last fledge) for each species.

trim_to_active

logical; TRUE or FALSE indicating if nest check data should be trimmed to include only those rows where the nest was active (in build, lay, incubation, presence of live young). Build status is considered when Nest.Status is "in" or "cn" (for incomplete or complete nest) but no eggs or young have been detected yet. The first check observing a fledge or fail event is retained, but subsequent checks would be targeted for flag/removal. Flag/removal follows mode. Note that this will include cases where a nest may have been abandoned, found after failure, found after fledging, or other cases of inactivity. See nw.filteractive to isolate checks to eggs and young only.

output

character; An optional character string to custom name the output dataframe

Value

dataframe

Details

This function calculates the number of days between First.Lay.Date, Hatch.Date, and Fledge.Date date values, comparing each to the user-provided acceptable date spans for each nest phase. Not all attempts contain these summary dates. An analyst may choose to explore nw.estclutchsize, nw.estfirstlay, nw.esthatch, and nw.estfledge functions to estimate these summary dates from the individual nest visit data prior to using this function. As an additional check, this function calculates the date span between the first occurrence of an incomplete nest, complete nest, observed egg, or observed young and last active date (either the last observation of eggs/live young or the first 0-egg/young count indicating fail/fledge) and compares this date span to the user-provided "total nesting period" value.

Examples

#' # Create phenology dataframe
phenology <- data.frame(species = c("carwre"),
                        lay = c(7),          # max observed
                        incubation = c(20),  # mean plus some extra
                        nestling = c(20),    # mean plus some extra
                        total = c(50))       # mean plus some extra

# Simplified NestWatch dataset with nest summary dates only
# Attemtp should be flagged for too long in incubation phase
data <- data.frame(Attempt.ID = c("A001"),
                   Species.Code = c("carwre"),
                   First.Lay.Date = as.Date("2026-05-23"),
                   Hatch.Date = as.Date("2026-07-14"),
                   Fledge.Date = as.Date("2026-07-30"),
                   Visit.ID = c(NA),
                   Visit.Datetime = as.POSIXct(c(NA)),
                   Nest.Status= c(NA),
                   Adult.Activity = c(NA),
                   Host.Eggs.Count = c(NA),
                   Host.Eggs.Present.Uncounted = c(NA),
                   Live.Host.Young.Count = c(NA),
                   Live.Host.Young.Present.Uncounted = c(NA))

nw.filterphenology(data = data,
                   max_phenology = phenology,
                   mode = "flag",
                   trim_to_active = FALSE)
#> ... Identified nesting attempts have been noted with 'FLAGGED' in the columns 'Flagged.Attempt' & 'Flagged.Check'.
#>   Flagged.Attempt Attempt.ID Species.Code First.Lay.Date Hatch.Date Fledge.Date
#> 1         FLAGGED       A001       carwre     2026-05-23 2026-07-14  2026-07-30
#>   Visit.ID Visit.Datetime Nest.Status Adult.Activity Host.Eggs.Count
#> 1       NA           <NA>          NA             NA              NA
#>   Host.Eggs.Present.Uncounted Live.Host.Young.Count
#> 1                          NA                    NA
#>   Live.Host.Young.Present.Uncounted
#> 1                                NA


# Simplified NestWatch dataset with nest visits data
# First and last checks should be flagged as inactive
data <- data.frame(Attempt.ID = c("A002"),
                   Species.Code = c("carwre"),
                   First.Lay.Date = as.Date("2026-05-16"),
                   Hatch.Date = as.Date("2026-05-29"),
                   Fledge.Date = as.Date("2026-06-14"),
                   Visit.ID = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
                   Visit.Datetime = as.POSIXct(c("2026-05-05",
                         "2026-05-13", "2026-05-20", "2026-05-25",
                         "2026-06-08", "2026-06-15", "2026-06-17")),
                   Nest.Status= c("no", rep("cn", 6)),
                   Adult.Activity = rep(NA, 7),
                   Host.Eggs.Count = c(0, 0, 5, 5, 0, 0, 0),
                   Host.Eggs.Present.Uncounted = rep(NA, 7),
                  Live.Host.Young.Count = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 5, 0, 0),
                   Live.Host.Young.Present.Uncounted = rep(NA, 7))

out <- nw.filterphenology(data = data,
                          max_phenology = phenology,
                          mode = "flag",
                          trim_to_active = TRUE)
#> ... Identified nesting attempts have been noted with 'FLAGGED' in the columns 'Flagged.Attempt' & 'Flagged.Check'.
